title: Deleting a profile destroys its entire library in one unguarded click
detail: The trash icon calls deleteProfile directly. profiles.remove cascades to every book, summary, blob and review card owned by that profile. No confirmation, no undo, no toast — one misclick on the profile picker permanently erases someone's whole library. The structural reason it is unguarded is that App.tsx renders ProfilePicker outside ConfirmProvider, so useConfirm would throw here. Meanwhile the much less destructive Reset All inside the app is properly confirmed with danger styling.

title: The library grid is mouse-only — book cards are divs
detail: BookCard is a <div onClick> with no role, tabIndex or key handler, and it is the sole means of opening a book from the library and from the stats drill-down. A keyboard or screen-reader user can search and filter their library but cannot open anything in it. Same defect as the stats cards (S112) and the PDF drop zone (S065), but on the app's primary navigation path.

title: BookCard already solves the broken-cover problem; BookDetail ignores the solution
detail: BookCard handles an empty URL up front and falls back to placeholderCover on error. BookDetail renders a bare with neither. The pattern exists in the codebase, is 4 lines, and is not adopted where it matters most — the full-width hero image.

title: CORRECTION to S136 — there IS scar tissue: a guard against the literal string 'null'
detail: `book.coverImageUrl === 'null'` defends against a code path that stringified null into the field. Nothing in the current codebase writes that, so it is a healed wound from the original AI Studio export. My earlier negative result was wrong because it only searched for TODO/FIXME-style markers, not for defensive comparisons — the more common form of scar tissue.

title: Priority badges and the rating chip are light-only
detail: getPriorityColor returns rose-100/700/200, amber-100/700/200 or blue-100/700/200 with no dark variants, and the Finished rating chip is bg-amber-50 / text-amber-700. On a dark card these render as pale blocks with mid-tone text.

title: Every card promises 'Read Masterclass' on hover, including books with no summary
detail: The hover overlay is unconditional, so an unsummarised Goodreads import advertises a masterclass that does not exist and cannot be generated (S135). The card body one line above correctly says 'Not summarised yet' — the two disagree on the same card.

title: A failed profile creation reports nothing
detail: try/finally with no catch: the spinner stops, the form stays filled, no profile appears and no message is shown. Third instance of this exact shape after GoodreadsImport (S120) and the ProfileView exports (S085).

title: Duplicate profile names are indistinguishable
detail: Nothing prevents two profiles called the same thing, and the list shows only the first initial and the name, so the only way to tell them apart is to open one and look at the library.

title: The key dialog can only set a key, never inspect, replace or remove one
detail: There is no way to tell whether a key is stored, no masked display of the current value, and no clear button — so a user with a revoked key has no path to remove it except clearing site data, which also destroys their library. This is the missing Settings surface that two error messages already point at (S139).

title: Key-error banner is light-only
detail: bg-red-50 / text-red-700 / border-red-100 with no dark variants, on a dialog that does flip to dark.
